title: Jesta says an attacker used the OpenCode AI agent against a financial firm and took a planted decoy key in five minutes and 44 seconds
date_note: Date of the Dataconomy article; the page gives the attempt as 16 November, which is before the map window, so the publication day is used.
geo_basis: Jesta's location as Dataconomy states it; the targeted firm is not named
summary: Dataconomy reports that Tel Aviv security firm Jesta saw an attacker use OpenCode, an open-source AI coding agent, against a customer, an unnamed financial services company. According to Dataconomy, the attempt began on 16 November and ended five minutes and 44 seconds later. Jesta said the attacker found and used an access key that Jesta had planted as a decoy inside a fake environment.
plain: A security firm says an attacker used an AI coding agent against one of its customers and took a fake key it had planted. According to Dataconomy, the attempt lasted five minutes and 44 seconds.
exec: Jesta says an AI coding agent found and used a decoy access key in five minutes and 44 seconds, per Dataconomy.
action: General advice: Dataconomy quotes Jesta's Finkelshtein as recommending that defenders watch visitor behaviour, not only threat feeds, and use decoy credentials and fake environments.

evidence.quote: The attempt began on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET and ended five minutes and 44 seconds later.

validation.note: Only Dataconomy was read; it relays Jesta's account. Jesta's own page was not found.
